prompt: After fitting GARCH(1,1) with normal errors, the standardized residuals still have a kurtosis of 6.
tells: standardized residuals still have a kurtosis of 6
why: GARCH explains some kurtosis, not all; use Student-t innovations.
trap: The leftover is in the tails, not the dynamics.

prompt: A QQ plot of standardized residuals against the normal bends away at both ends.
why: Heavy tails beyond the normal; switch to a fat-tailed distribution.
trap: It's the distribution, not the variance equation.

prompt: A 99% VaR from a normal GARCH model is breached on 3.2% of days in backtests.
why: Too many exceptions: the normal quantile is too thin; use Student-t (or skewed-t).
trap: VaR is the symptom; the error distribution is the fix.

prompt: Residual tails are heavy and the left tail is clearly heavier than the right.
tells: left tail is clearly heavier than the right
why: A skewed Student-t handles both heaviness and skew in the innovations.
trap: GJR handles asymmetric variance response, not skewed shocks.

prompt: The fitted Student-t degrees of freedom come out at ν = 5.
why: Low ν means heavy tails; as ν grows large the t approaches normal.
trap: Read ν as a tail-thickness dial.

prompt: You keep normal-likelihood estimates of the GARCH parameters but use robust standard errors, because residuals aren't normal.
why: Quasi-MLE: parameters stay consistent; Bollerslev–Wooldridge errors fix inference under fat tails.
trap: An alternative to switching the distribution.
